judge_edits_note: No value changed; the four stage-5 values are final, so no fresh proofread or fresh blind reader is required. TM: the four new en/tr pairs (ui-chrome nav.g.discover, nav.g.taste, nav.g.visit, nav.langChange) are to be appended to tr-translation/memory/tm.json by the orchestrator on merge; checked against TM: «Keşfedin» (footer heading) and the imperative «… bereketini tadın» (leisure dek) already stand in the TM, so no recorded pair is broken.

blind_disposition.obs: «Vahayı keşfedin» natural; slightly vague («the oasis» before the visitor knows what El-Ahsa is)
blind_disposition.reason: the source says the oasis (en «Discover the oasis», ar «اكتشف الواحة»); «El-Ahsa'yı keşfedin» would replace the source noun, and the site name already carries El-Ahsa on every page; «vaha» is the termbase generic noun.

blind_disposition.obs: «Tadın» homograph with the noun «tadın» (your taste); reads like a shop slogan; «satın alın» fits only the stores; suggested «Lezzetler ve alışveriş» or «Yeme içme ve alışveriş»
blind_disposition.reason: (1) Homograph: anticipated at stage 2; the parallel imperative «ve satın alın» fixes the verb reading in the same two-word line, and the possessive noun would be the sen-register «your taste», which makes no sense as a heading; the site already uses the imperative «tadın» in published text (TM: «… El-Ahsa'nın bereketini tadın»). (2) «satın alın» covering the stores only is the source's own split: «Taste» covers cuisine, dining and fruit, «shop» covers the stores (brief: the title must cover buying, not eating only). (3) Both remedies are noun phrases and break the one-form rule for the three titles and UI1-controls (a group heading of links keeps the source's part of speech, as the footer heading «Keşfedin» does; ar and en are imperative); «Yeme içme ve alışveriş» also repeats the item «Yeme içme» directly under it. (4) The longer imperatives that avoid «tadın» («Tadına bakın ve satın alın», «Tadın ve alışveriş yapın») add about 35–50px against 34px of headroom (1147 → about 1182–1197 > 1181). Nativeness docked 2 for the first-glance stumble.

blind_disposition.obs: «Ziyarete hazırlanın» natural, but confusable with the gold button «Gezinizi planlayın» (both imperatives about preparing the trip); suggested a noun label «Pratik bilgiler» / «Gezi öncesi»
blind_disposition.reason: all five readers (zh, de, ru, ur, tr) land on this title with the same two defects (near the nav.plan CTA; does not describe lodging + saved places). The Arabic pair «رتّب زيارتك» / «خطّط لرحلتك» carries the same closeness, so the Turkish keeps faith with the source. Within the source, the Turkish already takes the farthest faithful form: a different verb (hazırlanmak, not planlamak/düzenlemek) and no «gezi» noun. «Pratik bilgiler» and «Gezi öncesi» change the meaning (they name content the group does not hold, and «gezi» moves it toward the button); a noun for this title alone would break the one-form rule. Not deducted from the translation score.

blind_disposition.obs: register: imperative headings over noun items feel promotional; noun headings («Keşif», «Lezzetler ve alışveriş», «Gezi hazırlığı») more idiomatic
blind_disposition.reason: the source is imperative in ar and en; UI1-controls rules that group headings over link lists keep the source's part of speech (published footer headings «Keşfedin», «Planlayın»), so the menu and the footer speak with one voice; stage 2 tested the noun set («Vaha keşfi / Tat ve alışveriş / Ziyaret hazırlığı») and found it abstract. Taste, not a defect.

blind_disposition.obs: «Dil: Türkçe Değiştirin ⌄» reads as one broken sentence; capital D mid-line looks like a typo; formal imperative unusual; suggested «Dil: Türkçe» only or «Dili değiştir»
blind_disposition.reason: layout fact (JUDGE-NOTES, from the code): the row is two visually separate elements, «Dil: Türkçe» on one side and the control «Değiştirin ⌄» pushed to the far end (margin-inline-start: auto); the blind input joined them into one text line, which produced the broken-sentence and mid-line-capital effect. The control starts its own label, so the capital follows P9 sentence case. «Değiştir» is the sen imperative (forbidden by address_form); UI1-controls makes every control a polite-plural imperative (Kapatın, Kaydedin, Paylaşın); «Dili değiştir» adds «dil», which the source (en «Change», ar «تغيير») does not carry, and is sen. Dropping the label removes a source key.
